title: The first millennium CE, 1–1000 CE
reviewed: 2026-10-18. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: Rome destroys Jerusalem and its temple
events.summary: Roman legions take Jerusalem during the First Jewish Revolt. The temple is destroyed and never rebuilt.

source.quote: The siege of Jerusalem in 70 CE was the decisive event of the First Jewish Revolt

events.title: The Sasanian Empire is founded
events.summary: Ardashir defeats the last Parthian king. His Sasanian dynasty rules Iran until 651.

source.quote: ruled by the House of Sasan from 224 to 651 AD

events.title: The Council of Nicaea
events.summary: Bishops from across the Roman Empire meet at Nicaea. They issue the first form of the Nicene Creed.

source.quote: It met from May until the end of July 325.

events.title: Muhammad's emigration to Medina
events.summary: Muhammad leaves Mecca for Medina. The year becomes the start of the Islamic calendar.

source.quote: its date equates to 16 July 622 in the Julian calendar

events.title: The Dome of the Rock is built
events.summary: The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik builds a shrine over the rock on the Temple Mount.

source.quote: during the Second Fitna in 691–692 CE

events.title: The Abbasids build Baghdad
events.summary: Caliph al-Mansur builds a round city on the Tigris. It becomes the Abbasid capital.

source.quote: built by the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur in 762–766 AD

events.title: Vesuvius buries Pompeii
events.summary: Mount Vesuvius erupts and buries Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash.

source.wiki: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD
source.quote: In 79 AD, Mount Vesuvius

events.title: The Roman Empire reaches its greatest extent
events.summary: By the death of Emperor Trajan, Roman rule stretches farther than ever before.

quote: the Roman Empire reached its maximum territorial extent

events.title: The Edict of Milan
events.summary: Constantine and Licinius agree to tolerate Christians across the Roman Empire.

source.quote: the 13 February 313 AD agreement to treat Christians benevolently

events.title: Constantinople becomes the capital
events.summary: Constantine makes the old city of Byzantium his new capital. It stays a capital for 1,100 years.

source.quote: from 330 until its takeover by the Ottoman Empire in 1453

events.title: The last western Roman emperor is deposed
events.summary: Odoacer removes Romulus Augustulus. Many historians date the end of the Western Roman Empire here.

source.wiki: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
source.quote: In 476, the Germanic barbarian king Odoacer deposed the last emperor

events.title: Hagia Sophia is completed
events.summary: The emperor Justinian completes a great domed church. It becomes the largest interior space in the world.

source.quote: it was completed in AD 537

events.title: Vikings raid Lindisfarne
events.summary: Norse raiders sack the abbey on Lindisfarne. Many date the start of the Viking Age here.

source.quote: the Viking attack of 8 June 793 that destroyed the abbey on Lindisfarne

events.title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
events.summary: Pope Leo III crowns the Frankish king as emperor in Rome.

source.quote: In 800, Charlemagne was crowned emperor in Rome by Pope Leo III.

events.title: Aksum adopts Christianity
events.summary: Under King Ezana the Ethiopian kingdom of Aksum makes Christianity its state religion.

source.quote: adopted Christianity as its state religion in the mid 4th century under Ezana

events.title: Arab armies conquer Egypt
events.summary: The Rashidun Caliphate takes Egypt from the Eastern Roman Empire.

source.quote: took place between 639 and 642 AD

events.title: Igbo-Ukwu and the Kingdom of Nri
events.summary: Igbo-Ukwu becomes the capital of the Kingdom of Nri. Its artisans cast detailed bronzes.

source.quote: beginning in the 8th or 9th century CE

events.title: The Ghana Empire enters the written record
events.summary: The scholar al-Khwārizmī first names the West African empire of Ghana. It grows rich on Saharan trade.

source.quote: made by Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī in 830

events.title: The Kushan Empire forms
events.summary: The Yuezhi found an empire linking Central Asia and northern India along the Silk Road.

source.quote: formed by the Yuezhi in the early 1st century CE

events.title: The Gupta Empire
events.summary: The Guptas rule much of northern India. Science, art, and literature flourish.

source.quote: existed from the mid 3rd century to mid 6th century CE

events.title: Nalanda monastery is founded
events.summary: A Gupta emperor founds a great Buddhist center of learning. It draws students from across Asia.

source.quote: established by emperor Kumaragupta I of the Gupta Empire around 427 CE

events.title: The painted caves of Ajanta
events.summary: Monks and patrons carve and paint Buddhist caves in western India. Older accounts date this phase earlier.

source.quote: a brief period of 460–480 CE according to later scholarship

events.title: The Medieval Cholas rise
events.summary: The Chola dynasty of southern India begins its imperial age.

source.quote: achieved imperialism under the Medieval Cholas in the mid-9th century CE

events.title: Cai Lun improves papermaking
events.summary: A Han court official makes paper from bark, hemp, rags, and fishnets. Paper soon replaces bamboo slips.

source.quote: Cai's most noted innovation was in 105 CE

events.title: The Sui dynasty reunites China
events.summary: The short Sui dynasty unites China after centuries of division.

source.quote: ruled from 581 to 618 AD

events.title: The Tang dynasty begins
events.summary: The Tang dynasty rules China for nearly three centuries. Trade and the arts flourish.

source.quote: ruled from 618 to 907

events.title: Silla unites most of Korea
events.summary: Allied with Tang China, the kingdom of Silla conquers its rivals Paekche and Goguryeo.

source.quote: Paekche in 660 and Goguryeo in 668

events.title: Nara becomes Japan's capital
events.summary: Japan builds its first permanent imperial capital at Heijō-kyō, now Nara.

source.quote: a permanent imperial capital at Heijō-kyō, or Nara, in AD 710

events.title: The Diamond Sutra is printed
events.summary: A woodblock copy of a Buddhist text is printed in Tang China. It is often called the oldest surviving printed book.

source.quote: It dates back to May 11, 868 CE

events.title: Yijing visits Srivijaya
events.summary: A Chinese monk studies at Srivijaya on Sumatra. The kingdom is a center of Buddhism and sea trade.

source.quote: he visited Srivijaya for six months in 671 AD

events.title: Borobudur is built in Java
events.summary: Builders in central Java raise a vast Buddhist monument in stone terraces.

events.title: The Khmer Empire begins
events.summary: Jayavarman II declares himself universal king. The Khmer Empire grows to rule much of mainland Southeast Asia.

source.quote: conventionally dated to 802 AD

events.title: The First Turkic Khaganate
events.summary: The Göktürks overthrow the Rouran and found a steppe empire across Central Asia.

source.quote: 552) and his sons, succeeded the Rouran Khaganate as the main power in the region

events.title: The Battle of Talas
events.summary: Abbasid and Tibetan forces defeat a Tang army in Central Asia.

source.quote: Chinese prisoners captured at Talas in 751

events.title: Teotihuacan, the largest city in the Americas
events.summary: A planned city with great pyramids grows in the Valley of Mexico. At its height it is the largest in the Americas.

source.quote: (1 CE to 500 CE), Teotihuacan was the largest city in the Americas

events.title: The Moche of northern Peru
events.summary: The Moche build adobe pyramids and make fine pottery on Peru's north coast.

source.quote: flourished in northern Peru from about 100 to 800 AD

events.title: Tiwanaku at its height
events.summary: A highland city near Lake Titicaca leads the southern Andes.

source.quote: reaching a peak in 500-600 AD

events.title: Pakal the Great rules Palenque
events.summary: The Maya king Kʼinich Janaabʼ Pakal rebuilds Palenque. His tomb lies in the Temple of the Inscriptions.

source.quote: who ruled from 615 to 683

events.title: The southern Maya cities decline
events.summary: Tikal, Palenque, Copán, and Calakmul decline and are abandoned. The causes are still debated.

source.quote: went into decline during the 8th and 9th centuries

events.title: Chaco Canyon flourishes
events.summary: Ancestral Puebloans build great houses of stone in the American Southwest.

source.quote: Between 900 and 1150, Chaco Canyon was a major cultural center
